test_title: SSC Selection Post Matric Level Official Paper (Held On: 27 June, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In a circular race along a track of length 3600 m, X and Y run at speeds of 27 km/h and 45 km/h, respectively. Suppose they start at the same time and in the same direction, when will they meet again at the starting point?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed X = 27 × 5/18 = 7.5 m/s; Speed Y = 45 × 5/18 = 12.5 m/s.

Time for X to complete 1 lap = 3600 ÷ 7.5 = 480 sec.

Time for Y to complete 1 lap = 3600 ÷ 12.5 = 288 sec.

Meeting time at starting point = LCM(480, 288).

LCM(480, 288) = 1440 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 1440 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Track Length = 3600 m

Speed of X = 27 km/h

Speed of Y = 45 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Time to meet at starting point = LCM(Time taken by X for one lap, Time taken by Y for one lap)

 
 
• 
 START
 

 X (27 km/h)
 

 Y (45 km/h)
 Track: 3600 m
 Meeting at Start = LCM(TX, TY)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of X in m/s = 27 × (5/18) = 7.5 m/s

⇒ Speed of Y in m/s = 45 × (5/18) = 12.5 m/s

⇒ Time taken by X (TX) = 3600 ÷ 7.5 = 480 sec

⇒ Time taken by Y (TY) = 3600 ÷ 12.5 = 288 sec

⇒ Required time = LCM(480, 288)

⇒ 480 = 2⁵ × 3 × 5

⇒ 288 = 2⁵ × 3²

⇒ LCM = 2⁵ × 3² × 5 = 32 × 9 × 5 = 1440 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 1440 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting Anywhere on Track

To find the first time they meet anywhere on the track, use Time = Track Length ÷ Relative Speed. Same direction: Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. Opposite direction: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

LCM of Fractions

If lap times are in fractions, LCM(a/b, c/d) = LCM(a, c) ÷ HCF(b, d).</p
